ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is triangle ABC, there is a right-angle mark at C, and A is labeled 30°, so ABC is a right triangle with AB as the hypotenuse. Point D is located on hypotenuse AB, segment CD is drawn from C to D, and there is a right-angle mark at D, indicating that CD is perpendicular to AB. Reasoning: The bases of triangle BDC and triangle ADC can be taken as BD and AD respectively; they are both on the same straight line AB, and the heights from C to AB are the same, both CD. Therefore the area ratio [BDC]/[ADC] = BD/AD. Since triangle ABC is a 30°-60°-90° right triangle, and ∠A = 30°, BC = AB/2 and AC = (sqrt(3)/2)AB. By the projection theorem for the altitude to the hypotenuse in a right triangle, BD = BC^2/AB and AD = AC^2/AB. Therefore BD/AD = BC^2/AC^2 = (AB/2)^2 / ((sqrt(3)/2)AB)^2 = (1/4)/(3/4) = 1/3. So the required area ratio is 1/3.

method.method_draft: Read the diagram as a right triangle ABC with right angle at C, angle A marked 30°, D lying on hypotenuse AB, and CD perpendicular to AB. The text asks for [BDC]/[ADC]. Since triangles BDC and ADC use bases BD and AD on the same line AB and have the same altitude from C to AB, their area ratio is BD/AD. Use the 30-60-90 side ratio in triangle ABC: BC = AB/2 and AC = (sqrt(3)/2)AB. Then use the right-triangle projection theorem for the altitude to the hypotenuse: BD = BC^2/AB and AD = AC^2/AB. Therefore BD/AD = BC^2/AC^2 = (1/2)^2/(sqrt(3)/2)^2 = 1/3.

method.method_draft: Read from the image that ABC is right at C, angle A is 30°, D is on AB, and CD is perpendicular to AB. The desired ratio is [BDC]/[ADC]. Because BD and AD are collinear on AB and both triangles have altitude CD from C, [BDC]/[ADC] = BD/AD. Now angle B in ABC is 60°. In right triangle BDC, angle B is 60°, so angle BCD is 30°, giving BD/CD = tan 30° = 1/sqrt(3). In right triangle ADC, angle A is 30°, giving CD/AD = tan 30° = 1/sqrt(3), so AD = sqrt(3)CD.
